Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: [Adjusted from 1 to 0: no source URL available] Cross-border functionality exists but is primarily via traditional correspondent banking/SWIFT rather than integrated instant cross-border rails. No evidence found of Seychelles participation in PAPSS or a regional instant cross-border linkage for SEFT/mobile money after searches; cross-border payments therefore appear limited to standard bank wire channels.

revision_notes: Original score of 0 carried no cited source. A light check surfaced and confirmed via a fetched authoritative primary source (PAPSS official Payments Network Coverage document, June 2026): Seychelles does not appear among PAPSS live participant countries, extended-network countries, or 'live soon' markets. No other evidence of a regional instant cross-border payment linkage for Seychelles was found. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (No), since authoritative evidence of non-participation exists rather than a genuine absence of information.
revised_comments: Seychelles does not participate in the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) or any other identified regional instant/real-time cross-border payment scheme. PAPSS's official network coverage document (June 2026) lists live participant countries — including Djibouti, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe — plus extended-network and upcoming ('live soon') markets, none of which include Seychelles. Cross-border payments to and from Seychelles are consequently processed through conventional correspondent banking and SWIFT wire transfer channels rather than an integrated instant payment rail.

Definition: Whether digital payment systems and access points (apps, USSD, agents) are designed to accommodate persons with disabilities (visual, hearing, mobility, cognitive impairments), and disability-disaggregated coverage rates if data available.
Comments: No credible evidence found on specific accessibility requirements or accommodations for persons with disabilities in Seychelles digital payment systems (SEFT, mobile money apps, POS) or payment regulations after searching CBS consumer/financial inclusion pages and broader web for “accessibility”, “disability”, “inclusive design” + Seychelles payments.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 carried no cited source. A light check surfaced and a full fetch confirmed a directly relevant, authoritative trade-press report (Regtech Africa, November 2023) documenting the Central Bank of Seychelles' 'cash-lite' approach and specific accessibility accommodations already in place (talking ATMs, Creole-language ATM instructions, 24-hour call centres, fast-track bank lanes for elderly/disabled customers), alongside acknowledged ongoing gaps (PIN/card security concerns and limited smartphone accessibility for visually impaired users). Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (Partial), reflecting documented but incomplete accessibility provisions.
revised_comments: Seychelles' digital payment ecosystem offers some accommodations for persons with disabilities as part of the Central Bank of Seychelles' 'cash-lite' National Payment System Modernisation Plan. Measures already in place include talking ATMs, ATM instructions in Creole, 24-hour call centres for assistance, and fast-track service lanes for elderly and disabled customers at some banks, alongside targeted digital financial literacy sessions for vulnerable groups. The Central Bank, the government's Elderly and Disabled Division, and the Seychelles Bankers' Association continue to engage on outstanding barriers, including card/PIN security concerns and limited smartphone accessibility for visually impaired users, indicating partial rather than comprehensive accessibility.
